name: any-angle rod clamp, for diagonal reprap support

captions.detailed: This 3D model is a compact, octagonal-profile rod clamp designed for securing two intersecting rods. It features a central vertical screw hole through its octagonal body for tightening, with perpendicular semi-cylindrical cutouts on its underside to hold the rods. The outer edges of the octagonal prism are beveled, giving it a faceted, robust, and clean aesthetic suitable for mechanical assemblies.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric OpenSCAD script for an adjustable rod clamp that joins two rods at an angle. Users should be able to configure the rod diameter, wall thickness, screw diameter, gap between clamp halves, and toggle beveling on the outer edges.
captions.factory: The design is constructed using a 'clamp' module that defines one half of the assembly. This module starts with an 8-sided cylinder (using $fn=8) rotated and translated to form the octagonal main body. A difference() operation subtracts a series of rotated cubes to create the beveled outer edges, a cylinder for the rod channel (and an adjacent cube to form the open slot), and a perpendicular cylinder for the tightening screw. Finally, the main script instantiates and rotates the clamp modules to align them correctly, accounting for the configured gap.
